text.p: German publisher Bertelsmann on Sunday launched its Bertelsmann Interactive Studios with the aim of becoming Europe's number one in multimedia.

Bernd Schiphorst, president of the new unit, said in an interview the company would at first concentrate on the German market and would launch an online news channel with RTL television called "RTL Aktuell online". This would be complemented by a sports channel, he added.
"We will shortly announce a partner for the sports service. I am afraid that we haven't signed yet so I cannot reveal the name," Schiphorst said.
RTL Aktuell will have text, audio and video images and will be updated "up to the minute".

Bertelsmann is already 50 percent owner of the European AOL online service with America Online, but the German company is aiming for a wider audience on various platforms, be it the Internet or in combination with digital television.

Bertelsmann Interactive Studios, established just a few days ago, is at the moment 100 percent owned by the Hamburg-based media group which is also active in television with CLT and RTL as well as in music with the BMG label.

Schiphorst said that Bertelsmann aimed to seek international partners and would keep only a majority stake in the venture. He said the partners could be announced in the next few months. AOL International president Jack Davies told Reuters America Online was likely to become a partner.
In the next few weeks, Bertelsmann will announce a partnership with a so-called "search engine" company which has a programme that allows users to find information on the Internet.
"It is an existing company. A company like Yahoo!," he said. But he declined to indicate whether it would be Lycos, Alta Vista, Digital, Excite or any other of the mainly U.S.-based companies.
The deal with this company will allow Bertelsmann to fulfill its second goal of entering the British market beyond the AOL activities. Other countries will follow later.
"We want to make the online market a mass market. Go beyond the five percent of households who know it at the moment to the other 95 percent," he said.

To do that, Schiphorst wants to combine television with online activities. Before being appointed at the interactive studios, Schiphorst built up Bertelsmann's UFA television activities which are now being merged with Luxembourg's Compagnie Luxembourgeoise de Telediffusion (CLT).
"Television and online complement each other. This way, television will become an interactive medium," he said.

While he told a news conference on Sunday that "there will be no interactive television for another five years", he told Reuters that he expected the first combinations of television and the Internet in 1997, with people being able to send electronic messages to broadcasters over the Internet via the remote control of a television set.

For this he does not see himself limited to Bertelsmann related television companies such as RTL, CLT and M6 MTTP.PA and could ally which such broadcasters as France's TF1 and its Television par Satelitte (TPS) digital venture with France Telecom.
While reluctant to give any financial forecasts for the new activities, beyond its five million mark development budget, he said Bertelsmann was convinced of an enormous potential of the market.

"If you look at statements like the one from Intel boss Andy Grove, saying there will soon be more personal computers sold than televisions, if you look at our own figures, then you see that it will become a mass market," he said.

While AOL works on an subscription revenue basis, Bertelsmann Interactive Studios has advertising revenues as its main business model, be it through sponsorships for certain "web sites" or through straightforward ad pricing.
The start price is 100 marks per thousand "hits" on a page -- a "hit" being the moment that somebody visits a web page.
AOL Germany has 270,000 subscribers and in Europe the number will soon be over 500,000, he said.
